The problem you're closing
recruit â†’ billone physician, one program, many systems
Because Preferred Solutions runs the program and not just the placement, one physician moves through sourcing, an ATS, background and credentialing, onboarding, an HRIS, scheduling, payroll, benefits, and then feeds outcomes, FMV and a consolidated invoice back to the hospital. When those systems do not talk, the operations team re-keys the same person into each one, and credentialing alone can stall a start date by three to four months. Vorro is the integration layer that wires that stack together, any system to any system, so a physician's data and a program's numbers flow once instead of being retyped across every tool.

The Integration Pitch

Why Vorro, why Preferred Solutions, why now

Preferred Solutions is explicit that it is not locum tenens: it builds and then runs specialty programs, wrapping physician-led recruiting with credentialing, clinical oversight, FMV advisory, malpractice and consolidated billing that ordinary staffing firms never touch.

But running a program, not just a placement, means living across a stack of disconnected tools. A physician is sourced on a job board, tracked in an ATS, screened and credentialed in separate systems, added to an HRIS, scheduled, paid, and enrolled in benefits, while outcomes, FMV and the consolidated invoice have to be assembled back out of all of it, hospital by hospital and specialty by specialty.

That is where Vorro fits, and it is a modest, focused role rather than a rebuild. Vorro sits between the systems you already run and moves a physician's record from sourcing to credentialing to scheduling to payroll automatically, then rolls outcomes, FMV and billing back into one view, any system to any system. Onboarding becomes parallel not sequential, the consolidated invoice reconciles itself, and program KPIs are visible across every site. The honest first step is a short discovery call to map which tools you run today.
